persona: Owner or project manager at a company supplying hospital beds, trolleys, cabinets and ward furniture on project and tender orders

sections.h2: Why a furniture order behaves like a project
paras: Hospital furniture is rarely bought one bed at a time. A new hospital block, a ward refurbishment or a government tender produces a single order for hundreds of identical items, and that order is then released slowly, because the wards are painted and handed over in sequence. Software for hospital furniture suppliers has to hold one order against many part deliveries, so everybody can see what has gone, what is due and what has been billed.

The service story is also different from equipment. Beds, trolleys and cabinets are mechanical rather than electronic, so the obligation is usually a warranty with a stock of replacement castors, actuators, side rails and hydraulic parts, not a maintenance contract with scheduled visits. Aura Business tracks the order in phases, sends installation crews with job cards, and records warranty claims against the item and the ward it was installed in.

sections.h2: One order, a dozen deliveries, and no single view of it.
sections.lead: The order value makes the business. The margin is lost in transport done twice, items delivered to the wrong floor and installation labour standing idle.

items.p: After six part deliveries nobody agrees on how many beds are still due against the original order.
A consignment reaches a hospital where the ward is not plastered, and the stock sits in a corridor at your risk.

items.h: Challans and invoices out of step
items.p: Goods moved on challans over three months, and invoicing is reconstructed later from a pile of paper.
Assembly teams are sent without a list of what is on site, so half a day is spent finding cartons.
A bed fails in its second year and nobody can say when it was supplied or whether it is still in warranty.
Payment follows delivery and installation stages, and the paperwork proving each stage is scattered.

sections.h2: From the tender document to the last installed ward.

steps.p: The tender is tracked with its documents, deadlines and EMD, and the submitted rates are recorded for reference.
The award becomes a sales order with the full quantity, and the expected release phases are agreed with the hospital.
Purchase orders go to the manufacturer, goods are received into the warehouse, and stock is reserved against the order.
Each release goes out on its own delivery challan and e-way bill, and the balance against the order updates automatically.
An installation job is raised per ward, closed on the mobile job card with photos and the ward in-charge signature.
Tax invoices are raised against the delivered and installed quantities, and payments are tracked against the order.
Each supplied item carries its warranty period, and a claim later opens a job with the part replaced from spares.

items.q: Can one order be delivered over several months?
items.a: Yes. The sales order holds the full quantity and each release goes out on its own delivery challan, so ordered, delivered and pending quantities are visible on the order at any time without adding up paperwork.

items.q: Do we need AMC contracts for furniture?
items.a: Usually not. Most furniture obligations are warranty rather than scheduled maintenance, so the platform records the warranty period per supplied item and raises a job when a claim comes in. Annual contracts are available if you sell them on powered beds.

items.q: How is installation labour tracked across a large site?
items.a: Installation is raised as jobs per ward or floor, assigned to a crew with a date, and closed on the mobile job card with photographs and the ward in-charge signature. Offline mode covers sites without network.

items.q: Can we hold stock at the hospital site?
items.a: Yes. Create the site store as a warehouse location and transfer stock to it. Movements are recorded, so what is on site and what has been installed are separate and countable numbers.

items.q: Does it handle government tender supply?
items.a: Yes. The tender tracker holds documents, EMD and deadlines, rate contracts govern the price on repeat supply, and outcome analytics show your win rate by category. See tender management software.

items.q: How are replacement parts for beds managed?
items.a: Castors, side rails, actuators and similar parts are stock items with reorder levels, and a part used on a warranty job is issued against that job so stock drops and the claim history builds against the item.
